tasks.q: What type of connection is Ethernet?
tasks.fb: Ethernet uses cables, usually twisted pair copper or fibre.

tasks.q: What does an Ethernet frame contain so it reaches the right device?
tasks.fb: Each frame carries the MAC address it came from and the one it's going to.

tasks.q: What is the typical range of Wi-Fi?
tasks.fb: Walls and interference usually reduce this indoors.

tasks.q: What does a device need in order to join a Wi-Fi network?
a: A wireless NIC, and to be in range of a wireless access point
tasks.fb: The wireless NIC sends and receives the radio signals to and from the WAP.

tasks.q: What is the typical range of Bluetooth?
tasks.fb: Bluetooth is designed for devices close together.

tasks.q: Why is Bluetooth good for wireless earbuds?
a: It uses very little power, so batteries last longer
tasks.fb: Earbuds have tiny batteries, and they only need a short range and low bandwidth.

tasks.q: Does each feature describe Wi-Fi or Bluetooth?
tasks.fb: Wi-Fi is for networks; Bluetooth is for linking two nearby devices.

tasks.q: Which is an advantage of a wired connection over wireless?
a: It is usually faster and more reliable
You can use it anywhere in the building
It is easier to set up in an old building
tasks.fb: The other options are advantages of wireless.

tasks.q: Why is a wireless network usually harder to secure?
a: Its signals travel through the air, so anyone in range could try to connect or intercept them
tasks.fb: That's why Wi-Fi needs strong encryption, which is next lesson's topic.

tasks.q: A school hall needs 30 laptops online for one day. Which connection is best?
A server room needs the fastest, most reliable links. Which connection is best?
tasks.fb: Servers don't move, so cabled links give the best speed and reliability.

tasks.q: A wireless mouse for a laptop: which connection is best?
tasks.fb: Short range, low data and low power: a perfect fit for Bluetooth.

tasks.q: Does each statement describe wired or wireless connections?
items: Less reliable, and can be blocked by walls
Transfer speeds tend to be slower
Connections tend to be more reliable
More secure and easier to secure
Less secure and more difficult to secure
Sharing files tends to be easier
Users can access the network from anywhere in range
Less physically complicated and disruptive to set up
Transfer speeds tend to be faster
Sharing files tends to be more difficult
tasks.fb: Colour these on your worksheet: green for advantages and red for disadvantages.

info.title: Where Ethernet began
info.text: Ethernet was invented at Xerox's research lab in California in 1973. The same idea, much faster, still connects most wired networks today.

info.title: Wi-Fi's real name
info.text: Wi-Fi is the everyday name for a family of IEEE standards called 802.11. Each new version, such as Wi-Fi 6, is faster than the last.

info.title: A Viking king
info.text: Bluetooth is named after Harald Bluetooth, a 10th-century Danish king. Its logo combines the runes for his initials, H and B.

info.title: Checking frames
info.text: Every Ethernet frame ends with a cyclic redundancy check: a calculated value that lets the receiver spot if the frame was damaged on the way.

info.title: Li-Fi
info.text: Li-Fi is an experimental technology that sends data using flickering LED light instead of radio waves. It can't pass through walls, which makes it hard to eavesdrop on.

info.title: Mesh at home
info.text: Many homes now use mesh Wi-Fi: several access points that pass data to each other so the signal reaches every room.
